customManagers.description: Version pins annotated with a `# renovate:` comment in the Python constants, the legacy script, workflow shell blocks, and packaging/release-pins.env (pypi / github-releases / github-tags). The pins file is listed because two forges build this release — amd64 on Forgejo, arm64 on GitHub — and one file is what keeps their pins equal; a pattern covering only the workflows would silently stop bumping PyInstaller.

The Valetudo release-asset digests, each annotated with the release it came from. `github-release-attachments` resolves each arch's sha256 from the release itself, so a version bump carries its three digests in the same PR instead of leaving them describing the previous one. Each match spans ONE digest plus its own `# <version>` annotation: Renovate replaces currentValue inside the matched text, so the version has to sit within each dependency's own region, and the three regions must not overlap. Capturing one shared version for all three digests fails the whole branch update with 'currentValue not found in string to replace'.
sunxi-tools commit pins (Python constants, legacy script, both build workflows), tracked on the master branch.

Docker images pinned tag@digest inside a workflow `docker run` shell block, or in the files that carry such a pin outside a workflow: packaging/release-pins.env (the manylinux builders, nfpm and the smoke base, shared by both forges' build jobs), packaging/shellcheck-all.sh, and the two install/package smoke Dockerfiles, whose base images have to move with the qualification image ci.yml pins.

packageRules.description: These legs are compatibility FLOORS, not current-release aliases: the whole point is that a package which installs on the current release can still fail on the oldest one this project claims. Unclamped, Renovate bumps the tag and each floor quietly becomes a second current test — green, and proving nothing it was written to prove. Digests still refresh, so the images stay patched.
Docker Images

The smoke Dockerfiles' base images are claimed by the annotation-driven regex manager so they stay one dependency with ci.yml's qualification pin. install-smoke.Dockerfile carries the synthetic depNames (debian-13-current, debian-12-floor, ...) whose allowedVersions rules pin the compatibility floors; the built-in manager would see a plain `debian` instead and let those floors drift. Left enabled, the built-in dockerfile manager would also claim it as a separate `ubuntu` dep that updates in its own PR — and since publish.yml is the only thing that builds this file, that PR would automerge on a CI run that never touched it.
The Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04 legs are compatibility floors, not current-release aliases; Renovate still refreshes their immutable digests.
Debian 13 is the deliberately selected current qualification host; Renovate refreshes its digest but a new Debian release is reviewed before replacing it.
The Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04 legs are compatibility floors, not current-release aliases; Renovate still refreshes their immutable digests.
Ubuntu 26.04 is the deliberately selected current qualification host; Renovate refreshes its digest but a new LTS is reviewed before replacing it.
Fedora 43 remains the oldest supported Fedora until 45 reaches GA; Renovate still refreshes its immutable digest.
Fedora 44 is the deliberately selected current qualification host; Renovate refreshes its digest but a future Fedora is reviewed after GA before replacing it.
macOS 15 is the cross-architecture support floor; runner-image updates may refresh current hosts but must not silently drop the floor.
Python 3.11.0 is the literal source floor; Renovate must not move even its patch version and turn this into a current-3.11 test.

setup-python resolves a version through actions/python-versions' versions-manifest.json, which that repo merges over an hour AFTER publishing the GitHub release Renovate reads. A bump raised inside that gap installs nothing: every python job on both forges dies at setup with 'version not found', which reads as a broken PR rather than an upstream artifact that has not landed yet. Hold each bump until the manifest is certain to list it.
Rocky 8 and 9 are explicit maintained compatibility legs; Renovate refreshes their digests without relabeling either host.
Rocky 8 and 9 are explicit maintained compatibility legs; Renovate refreshes their digests without relabeling either host.
Rocky Linux 10 is the deliberately selected current RHEL-compatible host; Renovate refreshes its digest but a new major is reviewed before replacing it.
openSUSE Leap 16.0 is the deliberately selected qualification host; the registry's legacy 42.x tags must not be mistaken for newer releases.

Automerge patch, minor, and digest updates. Every dep that ships or builds the tool is exercised by a CI job (shellcheck / python / build / integration) and Renovate only automerges on green, so a breaking bump fails the PR before it can merge. Major updates, and the exceptions below, are reviewed by hand.

Valetudo is the firmware flashed to the robot, and its per-architecture digests have no datasource of their own. `packaging/refresh-pins.sh` recomputes all three from the bumped version as a postUpgradeTask, so the branch is complete when CI sees it.
prBodyNotes: `VALETUDO_SHA256` is refreshed automatically from the release assets; `test_constants.py` fails if a digest and its version comment ever disagree.

packageRules.description: sunxi-tools is the FEL transport compiled into every release and used against the robot's boot ROM. The pin IS the commit Renovate writes, so nothing else has to move with it, and every build channel compiles it before the gate goes green.
prBodyNotes: Every build channel reads this SHA from `src/dreame_valetudo/constants.py`.

packageRules.description: The macOS package compiles and signs tmux from its release tarball, whose digest has no datasource. `packaging/refresh-pins.sh` recomputes it from the bumped version as a postUpgradeTask.
prBodyNotes: `TMUX_SHA256` is refreshed automatically from the release tarball.

packageRules.description: This dep reads CPython's git tag, which has two consequences. The tag carries a leading `v` that no consumer accepts — setup-python resolves `python-version`, and the bundle build interpolates the value into a python.org source URL — so strip it. And the tag lands more than a day before actions/python-versions publishes the manifest setup-python installs from, so hold the bump until that manifest can serve it.

release-macos.yml's `python-version` is not a test runner: PyInstaller freezes that exact interpreter into the shipped .pkg, so it has to move with BUNDLE_PYTHON_VERSION and the checksum a human reviews alongside it. The annotation hands the line to the cpython tag dep; disabling the built-in manager here leaves that dep as its only owner rather than an automerging second one that could ship a different Python than the Linux bundles carry.

pyusb is the USB transport the fastboot client speaks to the robot. CI proves only that it imports and enumerates: the unit tests stub `usb.core`/`usb.util` into `sys.modules`, and the build-job client smoke stops at `find_device()` with no robot attached, leaving every descriptor, endpoint and bulk-transfer call unexecuted. Green CI therefore says nothing about the path that writes to flash, so a bump is read by a human.
prBodyNotes: CI cannot reach the flashing path, so green here does not cover the transport. The bench campaign is what exercises `dreame-fastboot` against real hardware.

packageRules.description: The dev toolchain lives in three places that must agree exactly: literals in the workflows, which CI installs with pip; `uv.lock`, which `uv run` resolves; and pyproject.toml, pinned with `==` rather than a `>=` floor. The floor matters because a satisfied one leaves `pep621` nothing to raise, so the lockfile cannot move in the same PR as the literals and each bump strands it. Pinned exactly, pep621 raises the bump and relocks `uv.lock` as an artifact while the annotated literals share the branch, so one PR carries all three and green proves the whole toolchain — which is what lets these automerge like any other CI-exercised dep.
prBodyNotes: `test_pinned_toolchain_matches_the_lockfile` fails unless pyproject.toml, `uv.lock`, and the workflow literals all name the same version. If this PR is red because Renovate could not relock, run `uv lock` and commit `uv.lock` here.

packageRules.description: CPython is frozen into the bundle, so a version change also moves the source checksum, and a new minor moves the Homebrew dependency with it. `packaging/refresh-pins.sh` does both as a postUpgradeTask, from the version Renovate just wrote.
prBodyNotes: `BUNDLE_PYTHON_SHA256` and `depends_on "python@3.x"` are refreshed automatically from the bumped version.

packageRules.description: These images define the shipped glibc ABI, so a bump stays hand-reviewed whatever the update type — the blast radius is every Linux package. The embedded-ELF check is NOT the manual part: packaging/check-glibc-floor.py runs inside deb.Dockerfile, which CI builds for x86_64 and publish builds for both arches, so a binary needing a symbol above packaging/glibc-floor.txt fails the build (at PR time for x86_64, at release for aarch64). What the human adds is judgement about the toolchain change itself, which no check encodes. Pinned to upstream's dated tags rather than `latest`: the digest alone already froze the build, so `latest` bought nothing and cost the reviewer the version needed to judge the bump at all. The regex versioning also confines candidates to dated tags, so `latest` is never offered as an update. Grouped because the two arches are one upstream release and move to the same dated tag together: reviewing them apart shows the reviewer half the change, and a toolchain skew BETWEEN the arches is itself the risk this hand-review exists to catch. Splitting them also doubled the rebase churn, since every merge rebases the other open PR and restarts its checks.
prBodyNotes: Held for hand review: the glibc floor check runs in CI, but no check encodes judgement about the toolchain change itself, and a skew between the two arches is the risk this review exists to catch.
